newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir blast kills at least two, wounds five.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir blast kills at least two, wounds five.

text.p: A car bomb killed at least two people and wounded five on Wednesday in Srinagar, summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state, a police official said.
"The bomb, planted in a car by suspected militants, killed two persons...," the official told Reuters.
The official, who asked not to be named, said the blast was near a heavily-guarded guest house that normally housed more than 200 government officials and state lawmakers.
He said the building was not damaged.
The injured included two policewomen, the official said. The identities of the dead and other injured were not immediately clear.
It was the fourth blast since a new state government, led by the state's National Conference party, assumed office after last month's local assembly polls, the first in nine years.
Kashmir's newly-elected chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, told separatist militants last week to surrender their arms within 30 days.
There has been no official response from the rebels.
Seven relatives of a campaign worker for the National Conference were killed in a blast on Monday, local news agencies reported.
Police and hospital sources say at least 20,000 people have been killed in six years of separatist violence in the disputed region. Abdullah has said the toll is closer to 50,000.
Dozens of separatist groups have been fighting for independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan since the revolt broke out in 1990.
Mainly Moslem Kashmir has been the cause of two of the three wars between India and Pakistan since the two nations won independence from Britain in 1947.
